body.text:
**M11 is verified and committed** (`f8f5e78`) — the query engine is done. The notable engineering in it: vector and keyword search scores can't be compared directly (L2 distance vs. bm25), so results merge by *rank* (reciprocal-rank fusion), which needs no calibration and naturally rewards chunks both halves agree on. Blame attribution uses real `git blame` plus a strictly read-only identity resolver — asking "why?" can never mint identity rows as a side effect. And synthesis degrades gracefully: with `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set you'll get a cited prose answer (Haiku 4.5 by default, overridable); without it, `ask` still returns the ranked sources — fully offline, still useful. I re-ran the whole core suite myself (237 passing) and personally read the API-key handling and failure paths before committing.

**Next is M12** — the thin CLI wiring that turns this into `git for-ai ask "..."` and `git for-ai blame --why <file>:<line>` — but it has to wait a beat: it needs `bin.ts`, which the review-UI agent currently owns. So the sequence is: review UI lands → I verify and commit it → M12 wiring (small enough that I'll likely do it inline) → then the first real dogfood of `ask` on this repo, which is the moment this whole system answers its founding question for the first time.

Both remaining pieces are close. When they land you'll have, in the same sitting: `git for-ai review` opening the live browsable UI, and `git for-ai ask "why did we eliminate the server ref-relay tier?"` answering from your repo's own captured memory.

Your caution is warranted — a globally-set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is visible to every process, and Claude Code does detect it and may offer to bill against it instead of your subscription. You should not have to set it globally, and I'll make sure you never do. Two things:

**First, the reassurance**: the key is entirely optional. Everything built so far — including `ask` once M12 lands — works with no key at all; you just get ranked sources instead of a synthesized prose paragraph. Synthesis is a garnish, not a dependency.

**Second, the fix**: I'm adding a git-for-ai-specific variable, `GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY`, checked *first* — a name Claude Code has never heard of, so it can't leak into your Claude Code billing:

attributes.command:
cd C:/src/git-for-ai/packages/core && pnpm build 2>&1 | tail -2 && pnpm vitest run src/query/synthesis.test.ts 2>&1 | grep -E "Tests |failed" && cd ../.. && git add packages/core/src/query/synthesis.ts packages/core/src/query/synthesis.test.ts && git commit -q -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Synthesis: prefer tool-scoped GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY over ANTHROPIC_API_KEY

A globally-exported ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is detected by every Anthropic
tool on the machine — including Claude Code, which may then bill the
API key instead of the user's subscription. The new env var scopes the
synthesis key to git-for-ai alone and is checked first;
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY remains a fallback for users who already export it
deliberately. Empty-string env values are treated as unset. Raised by
the project owner before any key was ever configured.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)"

summary: claude-code session: 12 tool execution(s), 2 model turn(s) for commit "Synthesis: prefer tool-scoped GIT_FOR_AI_ANTHROPIC_KEY over ANTHROPIC_API_KEY".
